deltadromeus:eswiki:8.title: Deltadromeus agilis (Filogenia de Deltadromeus como aveteropodo)

facts.statement: The genus Deltadromeus was described by Sereno and colleagues in 1996.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Sereno et al., 1996

facts.statement: American paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues described the genus Deltadromeus in 1996.
facts.quote: It was described by American paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues in 1996.

facts.statement: Fossils of Deltadromeus date to the Cenomanian stage of the Cretaceous period, approximately 100 to 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: This indicates that these fossils date to the Cenomanian stage of the Cretaceous period, 100-95 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Deltadromeus contains a single species, D. agilis, based on an incomplete postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, D. agilis, named based on an incomplete postcranial skeleton, the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Based on the holotype, Deltadromeus was approximately 8 meters long and weighed 1050 kilograms.
facts.quote: Deltadromeus was around 8 m in length and 1050 kg in weight based on the holotype.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus had relatively long forelimbs, proportionately longer than those of Allosaurus.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Deltadromeus are relatively long for a theropod, being proportionately longer than those of taxa like Allosaurus.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Deltadromeus had broad, quadrangular neural spines with pleurocoels that likely stored pneumatic air sacs.
facts.quote: Its tail vertebrae have broad, quadrangular neural spines (spines emerging from the base of the vertebra) with pleurocoels (cavities) which would store pneumatic air sacs.

facts.statement: Fossils definitively assigned to Deltadromeus were discovered in 1996 by Paul Sereno during an expedition in the Kem Kem Beds of eastern Morocco.
facts.quote: Fossils definitively assigned to Deltadromeus were first discovered in 1996 by American paleontologist Paul Sereno, who was part of a joint expedition by the University of Chicago and the Service Géologique du Maroc in an outcrop of the Kem Kem Beds known as Aferdou N'Chaft in Errachidia Province, eastern Morocco.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as SGM-Din 2, was an incomplete postcranial skeleton found at a single site.
facts.quote: The remains found consisted of an incomplete postcranial skeleton, cataloged as UCRC PV11 at the University of Chicago before being transferred to the Ministry of Energy, Mines and Environment in Rabat and catalogued as SGM-Din 2, that had been found in a single site.

facts.statement: The articulated holotype skeleton included dorsal ribs, gastralia, tail vertebrae, chevrons, forelimb fragments, a partial pelvis, hindlimb fragments, and hindfeet.
facts.quote: The skeleton was found preserved in articulation, one of the few articulated dinosaur skeletons known from the Kem Kem Beds, and consists of: two dorsal ribs, two gastralia ("belly ribs"), several caudal (tail) vertebrae, eight chevrons, an incomplete scapulocoracoid, incomplete forelimbs, a partial pelvis, two partial hindlimbs, incomplete pedes (hindfeet), and several additional fragments.

facts.statement: The specimen SGM-Din 2 was designated the holotype for Deltadromeus agilis.
facts.quote: The skeleton SGM-Din 2 was selected as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen of Deltadromeus agilis.

facts.statement: Egyptian fossils assigned to Deltadromeus were unearthed in 1911 and 1912 by Richard Markgraf during German expeditions in the Bahariya Formation.
facts.quote: These fossils, consisting of a left coracoid, pubes, right femur, an incomplete right tibia, and a left fibula, had been unearthed in 1911 and 1912 by Austro-Hungarian paleontologist Richard Markgraf and his crews during German paleontological expeditions to the Cenomanian-aged Bahariya Formation of northern Egypt.

facts.statement: Fossils originally described by Ernst Stromer as Bahariasaurus and later referred to Deltadromeus were destroyed in the Bombing of Munich during World War II.
facts.quote: All of the fossils described by Stromer, including those referred to both Bahariasaurus and Deltadromeus, were destroyed in the Bombing of Munich during World War II.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Deltadromeus and Bahariasaurus are distinct genera or if one is a synonym of the other.
facts.quote: Sereno and colleagues maintained that Bahariasaurus and Deltadromeus were different genera, but the validity and synonymy of the two genera is controversial.

facts.statement: Researchers cannot yet confirm if certain teeth belong to Deltadromeus due to a lack of fossil overlap and ongoing controversy about its classification.
facts.quote: However, the lack of overlap and the controversy surrounding Deltadromeus affinities made this impossible to prove until more fossils are found.

facts.statement: Originally classified as a basal coelurosaur related to Ornitholestes, this classification has been challenged by later studies.
facts.quote: Originally Deltadromeus was considered to be a basal coelurosaur related to Ornitholestes; however, later studies have challenged this idea.

facts.statement: Some studies have classified Deltadromeus as an avetheropod related to Gualicho or as a megaraptoran outside the family Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: Some studies have classified it as an avetheropod closely related to Gualicho or as a megaraptoran outside the family Megaraptoridae.

facts.statement: Some studies propose Deltadromeus is a ceratosaur, but its exact position within Ceratosauria remains debated.
facts.quote: Other studies have proposed that Deltadromeus is a ceratosaur; however, its position within Ceratosauria is debated.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus has been classified variously as a basal ceratosaur, a noasaurid, or an Elaphrosaurus-grade ceratosaur.
facts.quote: Studies have classified it as a basal ceratosaur, noasaurid, or an Elaphrosaurus-grade ceratosaur.

facts.statement: Many studies support the classification of Deltadromeus as a ceratosaur based on phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: Many studies find that it is a ceratosaur of some kind, supported by several phylogenetic analyses.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest Deltadromeus may be a junior synonym of Bahariasaurus, though this is not universally accepted.
facts.quote: Additionally, some studies have suggested that it may be a junior synonym of Bahariasaurus, another potential ceratosaur which lived around the same time and region as Deltadromeus.

facts.statement: If Deltadromeus is closely related to herbivorous or omnivorous ceratosaurs like Limusaurus, it may have been herbivorous or omnivorous.
facts.quote: If Deltadromeus is a ceratosaur closely related to the herbivorous/omnivorous Limusaurus and Berthasaura, it possibly would be herbivorous or omnivorous.

facts.statement: During the Cretaceous, North Africa was covered in mangrove forests and wetlands, supporting diverse fish, crocodyliforms, and pterosaurs.
facts.quote: North Africa at the time was blanketed in mangrove forests and wetlands, creating a hotspot of fish, crocodyliforms, and pterosaur diversity.

facts.statement: In 2001, Frank Seebacher estimated the holotype of Deltadromeus to be 8 meters long and weigh approximately 1050 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype individual was estimated to have measured 8 m in length and weighed around 1050 kg, slightly more than an imperial ton,by Australian researcher Frank Seebacher in 2001.

facts.statement: Specimens from the Bahariya Formation suggest a much larger size, with one femur measuring 1.22 meters compared to the holotype's 0.741 meters.
facts.quote: Assigned specimens from the Bahariya Formation come from a much larger individual, with the femur IPHG 1912 VIII 69 having a length of 1.22 m, compared to the 0.741 m femur of the holotype.

facts.statement: If Egyptian specimens belong to Deltadromeus, the genus could have reached lengths of up to 12.2 meters, comparable to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: These referred specimens, if the referral to Deltadromeus is validated, would indicate that members of the genus could grow up to 12.2 m in length, approximately the length of a Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated the combined Deltadromeus/Bahariasaurus size at 11 meters long and 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2016, American paleontologist Gregory S. Paul gave Deltadromeus/Bahariasaurus a length estimate of 11 m and a weight estimate of 4 MT.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus is known only from an incomplete postcranial skeleton that lacks most vertebrae, ribs, and forelimbs.
facts.quote: Deltadromeus is very poorly known, only being represented by an incomplete postcranial skeleton which is missing much of the vertebrae, ribs, and forelimbs.

facts.statement: The tibia-to-femur length-to-diameter ratio in Deltadromeus is 0.95, compared to 0.76 in Allosaurus and 1.16 in Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: The tibia/femur length/diameter ratio for example is 0.95 in Deltadromeus, whereas it is only 0.76 in Allosaurus and 1.16 in Ornithomimus.

facts.statement: The humerus of Deltadromeus is elongate with a deltopectoral crest that spans only one-quarter of the total humerus length.
facts.quote: The humerus is elongate with a relatively short deltopectoral crest that only spans 1/4 of the total length of the humerus.

facts.statement: The coracoid and acromion processes in Deltadromeus are broadly expanded front-to-back, a trait considered diagnostic for the genus and also found in fossils assigned to Bahariasaurus.
facts.quote: The coracoid and acromion processes are broadly expanded anteroposteriorly (front-back), a characteristic believed to be diagnostic of Deltadromeus that also appears in fossils assigned to Bahariasaurus.

facts.statement: The midshaft of the ischium in Deltadromeus is dorsoventrally compressed and features triangular obturator flanges on both the ischium and pubis.
facts.quote: The midshaft of the ischium is dorsoventrally (top-bottom) compressed, with triangular obturator flanges on it and the pubis.

facts.statement: The distal end of the ischium in Deltadromeus has a greatly expanded "foot" similar to basal abelisauroids, a feature seen to this extent only in an ischium assigned to Bahariasaurus.
facts.quote: At the distal end of the ischium, the ischial "foot" is greatly expanded, similar to those of basal abelisauroids but to an extent only seen in an ischium assigned to Bahariasaurus.

facts.statement: The femur of Deltadromeus is very gracile, with a shaft width-to-total length ratio of 0.074, similar to that of noasaurids.
facts.quote: Deltadromeus femur is very gracile, with a shaft width/total femoral length ratio of 0.074, similar to that of noasaurids.

facts.statement: An accessory trochanter on the distal end of the femur is unique to Deltadromeus, though its presence in a femur referred to Bahariasaurus suggests that specimen also belongs to Deltadromeus.
facts.quote: On the distal (away from body) end of the femur is an accessory trochanter (protrusion of the femur) that is unique to Deltadromeus, though a femur referred to Bahariasaurus has it as well, suggesting that this femur belongs to Deltadromeus.

facts.statement: The anterior caudal vertebrae of Deltadromeus possess broad, elongate, quadrangular neural spines, a trait absent in many theropods but present in ceratosaurs.
facts.quote: The anterior caudal vertebrae have broad, elongate, quadrangular neural spines (spines emerging from the base of the vertebra), a trait absent in many other theropods but present in ceratosaurs.

facts.statement: Many studies since its description have considered Deltadromeus to be a ceratosaur, though researchers disagree on the specific type of ceratosaur it represents.
facts.quote: Many studies published since the original description of Deltadromeus have considered it to be a ceratosaur, although different studies disagree on what kind of ceratosaur.

facts.statement: A 2003 study suggested Deltadromeus was a member of the Noasauridae, while other studies found it to be more primitive and possibly related to the ancestral ceratosaurs Elaphrosaurus and Limusaurus.
facts.quote: A 2003 study suggested it was a member of the Noasauridae, though others have found it to be more primitive, possibly related to the more ancestral ceratosaurs Elaphrosaurus and Limusaurus.

facts.statement: A 2016 study on noasaurid relationships found Deltadromeus, Limusaurus, and Elaphrosaurus all within the Noasauridae.
facts.quote: A more comprehensive study of noasaurid relationships published in 2016 effectively agreed with both of these interpretations, with Deltadromeus, Limusaurus and Elaphrosaurus all found to be within the Noasauridae.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis placed Deltadromeus as a noasaurid in every scenario, regardless of the Limusaurus specimen used, though the study did not include Gualicho or Aoniraptor.
facts.quote: A 2017 paper describing ontogenetic changes in Limusaurus and the effect of juvenile taxa on phylogenetic analyses placed Deltadromeus as a noasaurid in every analysis regardless of which Limusaurus specimen was used, although the analyses did not include Gualicho or Aoniraptor.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus was classified as a noasaurid in a 2020 review of the Kem Kem Group geology and fauna.
facts.quote: Deltadromeus was also considered a noasaurid in a 2020 review of the Kem Kem Group geology and fauna.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Deltadromeus is a distinct genus or merely a synonym of the poorly understood dinosaur Bahariasaurus.
facts.quote: In addition to the mysterious affinities of Deltadromeus, it may be a synonym of Bahariasaurus, another poorly understood dinosaur.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis suggested Deltadromeus and Gualicho were sister taxa within the family Neovenatoridae.
facts.quote: In their 2016 description of Gualicho, Apesteguía and colleagues found Gualicho and Deltadromeus to be possible sister taxa in the allosauroid family Neovenatoridae.

facts.statement: Some subsequent studies classified Deltadromeus as a ceratosaur, though they did not include Gualicho in their analysis.
facts.quote: Since then, some studies find Deltadromeus as a ceratosaur, but did not assess Gualicho.

facts.statement: In 2016, Motta and colleagues suggested Deltadromeus formed a clade with Aoniraptor and Bahariasaurus called 'Bahariasauridae' within Megaraptora.
facts.quote: Motta and colleagues (2016) suggested that Aoniraptor, a megaraptoran from Argentina, formed a clade with Deltadromeus and Bahariasaurus ('Bahariasauridae') that was distinct from Megaraptoridae within Megaraptora.

facts.statement: Delcourt and colleagues noted that the classification of Deltadromeus within Ornithomimosauria requires further study.
facts.quote: However, Delcourt and colleagues as well as a conference abstract recovered Deltadromeus and Gualicho within Ornithomimosauria in their phylogenetic analyses, with the former paper stating that the classification of the two needs further study.

facts.statement: A 2025 study noted that Deltadromeus lacks a femoral crest, a trait seen in ornithomimids like Struthiomimus and Gallimimus.
facts.quote: Delcourt and colleagues (2025) noted that Deltadromeus' femur lacks a crest seen in many other theropods, a condition observed in ornithomimids like Struthiomimus and Gallimimus.

facts.statement: The medial condyle of the Deltadromeus tibia bears a large process also found in ornithomimosaurs like Mirischia.
facts.quote: Additionally, the medial condyle of the tibia of Deltadromeus bears a large process found in the tibiae of ornithomimosaurs like Mirischia.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus is tentatively classified in the suborder Ceratosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ceratosauria?

facts.statement: Deltadromeus is tentatively classified in the superfamily Abelisauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Abelisauroidea?

facts.statement: Deltadromeus is tentatively classified in the family Noasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Noasauridae?

facts.statement: The species D. agilis was described by Sereno in 1996.
facts.quote: species_authority: Sereno, 1996

facts.statement: Deltadromeus fossils are found in the Kem Kem Beds of North Africa.
facts.quote: Fossils of Deltadromeus are known from the Kem Kem Beds, one of many dinosaur-bearing Cretaceous-aged geologic units in North Africa.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus fossils are also found in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt and the Elrhaz and Echkar Formations of Niger.
facts.quote: Others include the Bahariya Formation of Egypt and the Elrhaz and Echkar Formations of Niger.

facts.statement: During the mid-Cretaceous, North Africa was a mangrove-dominated coastal environment with vast tidal flats and waterways bordering the Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: North Africa during this period bordered the Tethys Sea, which transformed the region into a mangrove-dominated coastal environment filled with vast tidal flats and waterways.

facts.statement: Isotopic evidence suggests carcharodontosaurids and ceratosaurs in the Kem Kem Beds and Elrhaz Formation consumed sizable terrestrial animals.
facts.quote: Isotopic evidence supports this as there were greater quantities of sizable, terrestrial animals in the diets of carcharodontosaurids and ceratosaurs from both the Kem Kem Beds and Elrhaz Formation.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest niche partitioning occurred among theropods, with spinosaurids eating fish and other groups hunting herbivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: This over prevalence of theropods indicates that there could have been niche partitioning between the different theropod clades, with spinosaurids consuming fish while other groups hunted herbivorous dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Abelisauroid affinities suggest Deltadromeus may have been omnivorous or herbivorous.
facts.quote: The abelisauroid affinities of Deltadromeus and Bahariasaurus suggest that they may be omnivorous or herbivorous.

facts.statement: If omnivorous or herbivorous, Deltadromeus and Bahariasaurus may have filled a niche typically occupied by ornithischians.
facts.quote: This would indicate niche partitioning in the large theropods in these localities, with Deltadromeus and Bahariasaurus filling a niche typically filled by ornithischians.

facts.statement: The diet of Deltadromeus cannot be confirmed because no skull material has been found.
facts.quote: However, this cannot be confirmed no skull material has been found for either Deltadromeus or Bahariasaurus.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus was a carnivore with unusually thin hind legs for its size, suggesting it was a fast runner.
facts.quote: Este carnívoro tenía, los largos miembros traseros inusualmente delgados para su tamaño, sugiriendo que era un corredor rápido.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus was a cursorial animal with a small head, long neck, and long hind limbs.
facts.quote: Era un animal cursorial, con una cabeza pequeña, el cuello largo, así como los miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: The holotype of Deltadromeus agilis is a partial skeleton estimated to be about 8 meters long.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Deltadromeus agilis,almacenado bajo el número de catálogo del museo SGM-Din2 es un esqueleto parcial de un animal que se estima que midió cerca de 8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The living weight of Deltadromeus was estimated at around 1050 kilograms.
facts.quote: El peso del animal viviente se estimó en alrededor de 1050 kilogramos, un poco más que una tonelada.

facts.statement: Other estimates suggest a reduced weight of around 600 kilograms for Deltadromeus.
facts.quote: Aunque otras estimaciones apuntan a un peso más reducido, alrededor de los 600kg

facts.statement: Specimens referred to Deltadromeus were thought to come from a much larger individual with a femur 1.22 meters long, compared to the holotype's 0.74-meter femur.
facts.quote: Se pensó que provenían de un individuo mucho más grande , con una longitud del fémur, el hueso de la parte superior de la pierna de 1.22 metros, en comparación con el fémur de 0.74 metros de largo del holotipo.

facts.statement: If correctly assigned to Deltadromeus, referred specimens would indicate the genus could grow up to 12.2 meters long, roughly the size of a Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Estos especímenes referidos, si están correctamente asignados a Deltadromeus, habrían indicado que los miembros del género podrían crecer hasta 12,2 metros de largo, aproximadamente del tamaño de un Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: No cranial material has been found for Deltadromeus or Bahariasaurus.
facts.quote: No se ha encontrado material craneal para Deltadromeus o Bahariasaurus

facts.statement: Carnivorous teeth labeled as "Deltadromeus" are commonly sold in rock shops, but it is unknown if they truly come from this animal.
facts.quote: aunque los dientes carnívoros etiquetados como "Deltadromeus" se venden comúnmente en tiendas de rocas, no hay forma de saber si realmente provienen de este animal.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus fossils were discovered in 1995 by Gabrielle Lyon during an expedition led by Paul Sereno in the Tegana Formation of Morocco.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles del Deltadromeus fueron descubiertos en 1995 por Gabrielle Lyon, durante una expedición dirigida por Paul Sereno en la formación Tegana de Marruecos.

facts.statement: The single species Deltadromeus agilis, or "agile delta runner," is found in Kem Kem beds dating to the mid-Cretaceous Cenomanian, about 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se ha descrito un espécimen fósil de la única especie de Deltadromeus agilis o "corredor delta ágil", que se encuentra en las camas Kem Kem, que datan de mediados del período Cretácico en el Cenomaniense, hace unos 95 millones de años.

facts.statement: Sereno and others described Deltadromeus as a basal coelurosaurian in 1996, but Rauhut placed it within ornithomimosaurians.
facts.quote: Sereno y otros en 1996 describieron a Deltadromeus como celurosauriano basal, pero Rauhut lo ubicó dentro de los ornitomimosaurianos.

facts.statement: In 2003, Wilson and others proposed Deltadromeus was a noasaurid, while Carrano and Sampson in 2008 placed it as a basal ceratosaurian outside Neoceratosauria.
facts.quote: Más adelante en 2003, Wilson y otros postularon que era un noasáurido y Carrano y Sampson en 2008 lo colocaron como ceratosauriano básico fuera de Neoceratosauria.

facts.statement: Deltadromeus is often considered a ceratosaurian, specifically a member of the family Noasauridae.
facts.quote: Deltadromeus a menudo se ha considerado un ceratosaurio, más específicamente, un miembro de la familia Noasauridae.

facts.statement: In 2016, it was found that the South American theropod Gualicho shinyae shares many similarities with Deltadromeus.
facts.quote: En 2016, se encontró que un terópodo sudamericano conocido como Gualicho shinyae posee muchas similitudes con Deltadromeus.

facts.statement: Depending on the phylogenetic position of Gualicho, Deltadromeus may have been a neovenatorid carnosaur, a tyrannosauroid, or a basal coelurosaur if its close relationship with Gualicho is confirmed.
facts.quote: Dependiendo de la posición filogenética de Gualicho, Deltadromeus pudo haber sido un carnosaurio neovenatorído, un tiranosauroide o un celurosaurio basal si su relación cercana con Gualicho es confirmada.

facts.statement: There have been online suggestions that Deltadromeus is closely linked to Dryptosaurus, but Deltadromeus is considered a ceratosaurian or avetheropod while Dryptosaurus is likely a tyrannosaurid.
facts.quote: Ha habido sugerencias en línea que Deltadromeus estaría estrechamente vinculado a Dryptosaurus . Sin embargo, Deltadromeus es considerado un ceratosauriano o un aveteropodo, y Dryptosaurus es probablemente un tiranosáurido.

facts.statement: Longrich suggested that the "pubis" of the Deltadromeus holotype is actually an ischium.
facts.quote: El "pubis" del holotipo de Deltadromeus parece ser un isquion según Longrich.

facts.statement: A 2003 study suggested Deltadromeus was a member of Noasauridae, though others found it more primitive, possibly related to basal ceratosaurians Elaphrosaurus and Limusaurus.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2003 sugirió que era un miembro de Noasauridae, aunque otros lo encontraron más primitivo, posiblemente relacionado con los ceratosaurianos basales Elaphrosaurus y Limusaurus.

facts.statement: A 2017 document placed Deltadromeus as a noasaurid in all analyses regardless of the Limusaurus sample, although those analyses did not include Gualicho or Aoniraptor.
facts.quote: Un documento de 2017 que describe los cambios ontogenéticos en Limusaurus y el efecto de los taxones juveniles en los análisis filogenéticos ubicaron a Deltadromeus como noasáurido en todos los análisis independientemente de la muestra de Limusaurus, aunque los análisis no incluyeron Gualicho ni Aoniraptor.

facts.statement: In an Aoniraptor analysis, which may be synonymous with Gualicho, Deltadromeus was found with Aoniraptor and Bahariasaurus to form a likely unknown clade of megaraptorian tyrannosauroids distinct from Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: En un análisis de Aoniraptor, que puede ser sinónimo animal que Gualicho, Deltadromeus se encontró junto con Aoniraptor y Bahariasaurus para formar probablemente un clado todavía desconocido de tiranosauroides megaraptorianos diferentes de Megaraptoridae.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Deltadromeus as Noasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Noasauridae

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Deltadromeus in the family Noasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Noasauridae

facts.statement: Deltadromeus lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)
